Problem

`README.md` (verified at commit `c1a9acb`) documents the single-issue patterns well: each section under "How you use it" (line 17) carries the exact prompt in a blockquote. The project pattern, "A whole project, end to end" (line 56), is the exception: five numbered steps, no prompts, no mention that each step is a separate skill the operator invokes, and "While it runs, you are needed at three points" (line 78) describes the orchestration stage only, not the stages before it. A reader who finishes the README knows the project flow exists and cannot start it.

The principle underneath both patterns is stated nowhere in operator terms: **GitHub is the state.** Every stage reads its inputs from the issue, its comments, labels and linked PRs, and writes its outputs there, so any stage can be run by a fresh session, and stopping a session and starting a new one for the next stage is the normal move, not a recovery. "Why it compounds" (line 110) gets close ("the output of one step is the reliable *input* of the next") and names token cost, but never says the operator-facing consequence: you can, and should, hand off between stages. The design doc states it as R20 for the orchestrator alone.

## Proposed approach

Three edits to `README.md`, no new file:

1. **Rewrite "A whole project, end to end"** so each stage reads like the single-issue sections: what state it starts from, the prompt in a blockquote, which skill fires, what you are asked, what state it leaves. The stages and prompts:

   | Stage | You say | Skill | Leaves |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Design | "file this as a tracking issue" (in the session that discussed it) | `issue-workflow` | tracking issue with stable IDs |
   | Design review | `review <URL> as a spec` (reviewer session) | `issue-reviewer`, design mode; author session answers rounds | design-mode `READY` |
   | Acceptance | you sign off | `issue-workflow` records the row | acceptance row in the decision log |
   | Decomposition | `decompose <URL>` (fresh session) | `issue-workflow` | children, blocked-by links, `project:<slug>` |
   | Set review | `review the set on <URL>` (reviewer session) | `issue-reviewer` | every child `READY` |
   | Orchestration | `orchestrate <URL>` (fresh session) | `orchestrate` | closeout PR; you merge; the parent closes |

   Keep the existing paragraph's substance (what the set review checks, the decision-log write-back, what closeout produces) under the stages it belongs to. Keep the pointer to https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/223 as the worked example.

2. **A short section, "GitHub is the state"**, placed between "How you use it" and "Why it compounds". Four or five sentences: every stage's inputs and outputs are on the issue (body, comments, labels, sub-issue and blocked-by links, linked PRs); nothing a stage needs lives in the session that ran the previous one; so each stage can run in a fresh session, and the plugin recommends that at every stage change because the session that wrote a design is the most expensive one to keep alive; a session that dies mid-stage is restarted with the same prompt and resumes from GitHub. Name the two things that are *not* on GitHub and why (retrospectives and follow-up entries, which are local by design and read by `process-review` and `followup-review`), so the claim is exact.

3. **The operator's touchpoints, across the whole flow**, replacing the "three points" sentence: deciding that a discussion is a project, signing off the design, answering escalations, merging each PR, and approving follow-up issue text at closeout. If https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/404 has landed, add its operator check before review to the list; if not, leave it out rather than describing unshipped behavior.

The prompts in the table are the trigger phrases the skill descriptions carry today. If https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/405 has landed, the stage sections can say "the previous stage prints this prompt for you" in one clause; if https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/406 has landed, "GitHub is the state" names its skill as the way to ask where a project stands. Neither is required for this issue; the README documents what is shipped at the time of writing, and `issue-workflow`'s "Maintaining issues" sweep covers the rest.

Rejected: a separate `docs/flows.md`. The README is where a newcomer reads, and the single-issue patterns live there; splitting the project pattern out would make it the one flow a reader has to go looking for. Rejected: describing the flow from the design doc. That document is the implementer's record (44 KB, written in requirement IDs) and is linked from the closeout; the README is the operator's.

## Open questions / decisions for the implementer

- **Q1. Regenerate a demo GIF for the project flow?** Default: no. `docs/media/demo-orchestrate.sh` already shows the orchestration stage; the earlier stages are text-shaped and a table reads better than a recording.
- **Q2. Does `docs/configuration.md` or `docs/maintainers.md` need a matching change?** Default: no; `docs/maintainers.md` already names where the tracking-issue conventions live.

## Acceptance criteria

- "A whole project, end to end" carries a blockquoted or tabled prompt for every stage in the table above, and each prompt matches a trigger phrase in the corresponding skill's `description:` at the merge commit (`orchestrate`, `issue-workflow`, `issue-reviewer`).
- A section headed "GitHub is the state" exists between "How you use it" and "Why it compounds" and names retrospectives and follow-up entries as the local exceptions.
- The operator touchpoints list covers the stages before orchestration, not only the three the current sentence names.
- `docs/media/check-render.sh` passes, since the README's rendered output is CI-checked.
- Changelog fragment present, or `no-changelog` with the reason that the plugin's behavior is unchanged.

## Required reading

- `README.md`, "How you use it" through "Why it compounds" (lines 17 to 180).
- `dnbg-workflow/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md`, `dnbg-workflow/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md` and `dnbg-workflow/skills/issue-reviewer/SKILL.md`, the `description:` line of each, for the exact trigger phrases.

## Related (optional, do not read unless blocked)

- https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/405 (stage exits print the next prompt), https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/406 (`project-status` lookup), https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/407 (recognising a project at creation time): the three changes this README describes the shipped state of, whichever have landed.
- https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/404, the operator check before review, an operator touchpoint to add once shipped.
- `docs/design/planning-and-orchestrating-multi-issue-projects.md`, R20 and "Goals", the design's own statement of statelessness and operator attention.
